matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns inflated sample efficiency metrics in Figure 6(b) that are inconsistent with the learning curves in Figure 6(a). Pred 4 identifies an inconsistency between Figure 6(b) and Appendix Table 2 (ablation results), which is a different comparison involving different data sources. These are distinct scientific issues.

Both identify a sign error in the f^{return} formula in Section 3.1. GT 2 describes the advantage weighting sign error making the gradient ascent misaligned with stated goals. Pred 1 explicitly identifies the minus sign in the advantage term and explains how it contradicts the claimed interpretation. Same underlying issue.

GT 3 concerns the failure to disclose which specific p value was used for each environment in the main results (Section 5.2), creating unfair comparison through selective hyperparameter reporting. None of the findings address this specific issue of non-disclosure of environment-specific p values in the main results.

GT 4 concerns overclaiming in the abstract about 'eliminating' sample inefficiency and 'completely solving' training instability, when results show only partial improvements. None of the findings address exaggerated claims in the abstract about elimination vs. improvement.

GT 5 concerns fabricated or premature citations (Cheng et al., 2025; Deng et al., 2025) in Section 6. Pred 3 identifies a fabricated citation 'Kumar et al. [2024]' in the Introduction with no reference list entry. Both identify the same type of issue (fabricated citations), though at different locations.

GT 6 concerns the omission of ethical considerations and failure mode discussions for the safety-critical LLM application in Section 5.3 and the Limitations section. None of the findings address missing ethical or safety discussions.

GT 7 concerns inappropriate marketing-style language and rhetorical exaggeration in the Introduction (e.g., 'completely solves,' 'unprecedented,' 'revolutionary breakthrough'). None of the findings identify rhetorical manipulation or promotional language issues.

Both identify contradictory statements about the reference policy π^{ref} in Section 3.1. GT 8 notes the contradiction between setting π^{ref} = π_{θ^{(k)}} (dynamic) vs. Appendix A.2's 'fixed reference policy.' Pred 2 identifies the same contradiction between 'fixed, pre-trained policy' and 'dynamic reference evolves with training.' Same underlying issue.

GT 9 concerns manipulation of y-axis ranges in Figure 6(a) to visually amplify differences (e.g., selective cropping, narrow ranges). None of the findings address visual encoding manipulation or selective axis range choices in the learning curves.

GT 10 concerns unfair experimental comparison where IIF benefits from environment-specific hyperparameter optimization (various p values) while baselines use default hyperparameters without similar tuning. None of the findings address this asymmetric experimental design issue.

GT 11 concerns claims of 'consistent improvement' in Section 5.2 despite wide confidence intervals and evidence of performance degradation in some rounds. None of the findings address cherry-picking favorable interpretations while downplaying high variance or inconsistent results.

GT 12 concerns the missing learning rate η_j in the influence score formula and inconsistent use of θ_j^{(k)} notation in Section 3.1. None of the findings identify the missing learning rate term or notational inconsistency in the influence calculation formula.

GT 13 concerns potential selective reporting of only successful environments in Section 5.2, with negative results possibly hidden (e.g., failure cases mentioned only in appendices). None of the findings address selective environment reporting or missing negative results.

GT 14 concerns misattribution of the f^{return} formulation to Sutton and Barto Section 13.4, conflating standard REINFORCE with their novel construction. None of the findings address this specific misattribution of established theory or incorrect citation of Sutton and Barto.

GT 15 concerns contradictory claims about computational overhead between Section 5.1 ('negligible overhead') and detailed timing data in Appendix B.9/Table 5-6 showing substantial costs (7-15% overhead, exceeding forward passes in LLM setting). None of the findings address this contradiction about computational cost claims.
